body:
**Status: tooling improvement (verification engineering). No new κ, and no mathematical check is changed or weakened.**

Track 85–94 (verification engineering), assignment seed 86 (OS CSPRNG via Python `secrets`). Base commit `2921874911956718fcaaaf9396fe8267b3cfa9f0`.

## What it speeds up

In the selected T37 replay (`research/community-frontier942-audit/STAGES.json`), the exact U8 phase lowering `phases_full.py` takes **154.3 s of 403 s (38%)**. It lowers 1,005 frames, 2,949 directed edges and 224 endpoint adapters, and every edge and adapter is an independent, pure computation of the pinned `clifford_exact.py`.

`research/phase-recipes-parallel/phases_parallel.py` is an opt-in drop-in with the same arguments plus `--jobs` and `--engine`:
- The parent runs the frame loop with all of its assertions.
- Workers run the **unchanged pinned functions** per edge and adapter, including the per-edge rank assertion.
- Results are collected in serial order. Nothing is written unless every worker succeeds.
- `CLIFFORD-RECIPES.json` is **byte-identical**: digest `4629507d…`, the pin in PR870's `LOCAL-PINS-barch-U8.json`.
- `--engine dense662` additionally installs the merged PR662 exact evaluator (pinned by digest) as `Op.zero_state`, exactly as PR662's own `run.py` does.

## Benchmark (same pinned input, one machine: macOS arm64, 10 cores, Python 3.14.8)

| Runner | Wall time | Speedup |
|---|---:|---:|
| pinned serial `phases_full.py` via `run_portable.py` | 92.2 s | 1× |
| parallel, 10 jobs, reference engine | 16.2 s | **5.7×** |
| PR662 evaluator alone, 1 job | 12.3 s | 7.5× |
| parallel, 10 jobs, PR662 evaluator | 3.2 s | **28.8×** |

All runs produced the pinned bytes. Receipt: `BENCHMARK-macos-arm64.json`.

## Relation to #1029 (aliromman, opened shortly before this)

#1029 speeds up the same step with a new sparse evaluator: 16.4× against the original on another machine. This PR is complementary.
- **Equivalence by construction.** The default engine uses only unchanged pinned code, so only process scheduling differs.
- **Composition.** The parallel layer multiplies whichever per-edge evaluator is installed. With the already-merged PR662 evaluator it reaches 28.8× here; #1029's evaluator could be plugged in the same way if accepted.

## Coverage and controls

- Every frame, edge and adapter assertion of the serial loop runs.
- C1: a corrupted frame fails in the parent, and no output is written.
- C2: an edge between two equal-rank frames fails inside a worker under both engines. The run exits non-zero without writing recipes, and the pinned serial script rejects the same input at the same assertion.
- `CLIFFORD-REVIEW.json` equals the archived review apart from elapsed seconds.

## Reproduce

```sh
make phase-recipes-parallel-verify      # about 25 s: both engines in parallel, pins, controls, tests
make phase-recipes-parallel-benchmark   # about 2 min: adds the serial reference and the one-job PR662 timing
```

Expected: `PASS_PHASE_RECIPES_PARALLEL`. Standard-library Python 3.10+, no network. The input word is read in memory from the pinned T37 archive and checked against PR870's pin.

## Scope

- Opt-in. The serial path in `reproduce_barch.py` / `scripts/verify_frontier942.py` remains the default and is not modified. `reproduce_barch.py --skip-phases` plus this runner gives the integration path, which is left to the maintainers.
- Only this step is accelerated; `layer-end-controls` (77 s) is untouched.
- The timings are local measurements.

title: Tooling: opt-in parallel exact U8 phase recipes, byte-identical; 5.7x alone, 28.8x with merged PR662 evaluator (no new kappa)
